chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying:

Gabriel descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Muhammad! Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — conveys His greetings to you and says: 'I have prohibited the Fire upon the loins that bequeathed you, the womb that carried you, and the lap that adopted you.'

So he said: O Gabriel! Clarify that for me. He said: As for the loins that bequeathed you, that is Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. As for the womb that carried you, that is Amina bint Wahb. As for the lap that adopted you, that is Abu Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Fatima bint Asad.

key_terms.بَطْن: Womb — the mother who carried and bore the Prophet
key_terms.جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ: Mighty is His Majesty — a formula of divine praise
key_terms.حَرَّمْتُ النَّار: I have prohibited the Fire — divine exemption from hellfire, a rare honor
key_terms.حِجْر: Lap/embrace — the one who adopted and raised the Prophet after his parents' deaths
key_terms.صُلْب: Loins — the paternal biological line through which lineage is transmitted

ai.seo_question: Did Abu Talib die as a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated via a chain reaching Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reports a divine message delivered by the angel Gabriel to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), declaring that God has exempted from hellfire the four forebears who nurtured the Prophet: his father Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (the loins), his mother Amina bint Wahb (the womb), and his paternal uncle Abu Talib and Abu Talib's wife Fatima bint Asad (the lap/embrace). This hadith is highly significant in Shia theology as it affirms the faith and salvation of Abu Talib, a position contested in Sunni tradition but firmly held in Shia scholarship. The triple metaphor of 'loins, womb, and lap' emphasizes the complete physical and social care that surrounded the Prophet from before his birth.
